cells.uncertainty: Eight C JSON third-party paths pass two valid controls with format-aware tree results, parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback. The original Conan recipe search missed Debian-packaged C parsers; a bounded Debian source-name search for 'json' (320 hits) plus exact lookups for jansson, jq, frozen, jsmn and parson in the same hashed popcon snapshot found the Debian-packaged C parser leads. libfastjson is a json-c fork and shares the json-c tokener family; jq's count is the jq source package (mostly the command-line program), and its jv C API is documented on the project wiki without a stability commitment; jq numbers have one kind, so integer/float in its tree comes from the preserved decimal literal. frozen fails the nested-object control (\u00e9 decoded to one Latin-1 byte), jsmn is tokenizer-only, and liblaxjson (1 installation) and parson (no Debian source) remain unselected. Debian installations mostly reflect dependencies and miss vendored copies. These paths do not establish a definitive top ten or full RFC 8259 compliance. ISO C documents no JSON API.

Ten C++ JSON package paths pass two valid controls with scoped parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback. Glaze uses a generic_i64 DOM and a parser-only probe; POCO JSON reaches its ParserImpl and bundled pdjson tokenizer with a parser-only probe. jsoncons uses the insertion-ordered ojson tree and a parser-only probe whose AFL++ allowlist names the basic_json_parser methods, because a file-only allowlist dropped parser functions whose first instruction is inlined from another header; PicoJSON and taoJSON use the same function-scoped allowlist approach. PicoJSON and taoJSON store objects in std::map, so their trees lose source key order: their controls check array order and integer/float kinds exactly but compare object members by key. taoJSON runs its own grammar on the separately pinned PEGTL 3.2.6 engine, and its 1.0.0-beta.14 tag is an upstream pre-release; no final 1.0.0 exists. The lowest ranks rest on weak signals: PicoJSON 16 installations (0 recent), jsoncons 3 (1 recent), and taoJSON 2 (both no_files). Glaze has 171 comparable Debian source-package installations, but the source metric favors runtime packages and undercounts header-only libraries. Boost.JSON and POCO have no JSON-specific Debian source count and remain primary-unranked; POCO's 190 libpoco-dev installs are suite-wide, while its component runtime 125 are all classified no_files. One documentation lead remains unresolved: Qt. The 320 JSON-name source hits exclude Glaze, found by a supplementary exact source-name lookup. No complete top-ten claim follows. Two small valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259, numeric boundaries, other encodings, or malformed-input behavior.

Ten Go JSON package paths pass two valid structure-aware controls with parser-source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: json-iterator/go (18,454 Imported by), tidwall/gjson (10,420), ugorji/go/codec (10,142), goccy/go-json (4,192), mailru/easyjson/jlexer (3,424), bytedance/sonic (2,428), buger/jsonparser (2,171), valyala/fastjson (895), go-faster/jx (451), and segmentio/encoding/json (348). Sonic uses its own Go optdec plus native NEON parser on pinned linux/arm64 Go 1.27.1; Go line coverage and AFL feedback omit NEON assembly instructions. segmentio/encoding/json uses its own parse.go tokenizer and decoder; it imports encoding/json only for shared types. easyjson jlexer is used through its documented generic Lexer.Interface rather than generated code; its Imported by count mostly reflects generated code. go-faster/jx is a lightweight fork of json-iterator with rewritten decoder code and no import of json-iterator or encoding/json; its lineage is shared with the selected json-iterator path. GJSON and buger/jsonparser are path-query parsers; only GJSON has a full-document validator in its harness. go-codec is multi-format and its Imported by count is not JSON-specific. Ten paths reach the ceiling; go-structform/json and gojay remain unresolved leads and the k8s util/json and go-json-experiment paths share the standard encoding/json lineage, so ranks are among verified paths only. Search was bounded to five pkg.go.dev queries of 100 hits each. The standard encoding/json path remains separate and unranked. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell: ten JSON package/API paths are control-verified and runnable. Jackson databind and core share a tokenizer family; Gson, fastjson 1.x, org.json, fastjson2, json-simple, json-smart, Moshi, and Parsson are separate parser families. Fastjson 1.2.83 has its own DefaultJSONParser/JSONLexer; the com.alibaba:fastjson coordinate adoption metric sums both 1.x and later 2.x fastjson2 facade releases, so it is not a 1.x-only count. Its pinned-release direct-dependent count is separately recorded. Json-simple 1.1.1 is an older 2012 release with a high default-release count, so ranking uses the common deps.dev summed metric. Json-smart is verified on its RFC 4627 object/array mode, not scalar roots. Parsson implements Jakarta JSON-P with its own tokenizer over a local InputStream; the Jakarta API jar supplies interfaces. Three numeric leads remain unverified. Maven Central search is bounded to 100 hits per query (322 unique hits); deps.dev counts measure package adoption, not JSON-specific use. Two valid nested controls do not establish complete format coverage.

Pilot cell: ten high-download package/API paths have valid nested-object and nested-array controls, package parser coverage, and AFL++ feedback; nine parser families are represented. jsonparse (105,362,611 downloads) has no API in its README; Parser.write(Buffer) is evidenced by packaged examples and tests. The adapter requires one root and checks the parser stack and tokenizer state. JSONStream (56,299,470 downloads) is a separate stream API path over the same pinned jsonparse 1.3.1 tokenizer, not an independent engine. JSONStream.parse([]) emits one root according to packaged code and tests despite its README statement. Its private parser exposes no end-of-input completeness check: the adapter requires one emitted root, no error, and stream end, but trailing unfinished syntax after a complete root may go undetected. JSONStream own package source is covered; differential feedback on the valid controls arises only in underlying jsonparse source. @humanwhocodes/momoa (18,038,222 downloads) has a documented string API only: the adapter decodes local bytes as strict UTF-8 and calls parse(text, {mode: 'json'}), which rejects tokens after the first value; the summary is taken from its AST nodes. @streamparser/json receives the entire Buffer and checks trailing bytes after the first root for whitespace. json5 is a JSON5 superset parser with its own lexer and state machine. It parses both valid strict JSON controls exactly through a documented text API, but accepts JSON5-only syntax and its high download count mainly reflects configuration-file use. json-bigint also has a documented string API: the adapter decodes local bytes strictly, then tags the parser's returned tree. Its Crockford-derived parser source is distinct from the other selected families; BigNumber behavior for long numeric tokens is not established by these controls. jsonc-parser adds a strict-option parseTree text API over its own Microsoft scanner/tree parser; both valid controls match but do not test JSONC extension rejection. lossless-json independently parses strict local UTF-8 text into type-tagged values whose numeric lexemes remain exact LosslessNumber strings; the two valid controls show parser-source coverage and stable input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Other high-download leads remain unresolved. Downloads cover 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. Standard JSON.parse is separate. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Nine PHP JSON third-party paths passed valid nested object controls and source-line coverage. Laminas, JSON Machine, salsify, pcrov and the four paths added from the extended search (boundwize/jsonrecast, laktak/hjson, klkvsk/json-decode-stream, eftec/services_json) also passed a valid nested array control and stable source-line AFL feedback. Laminas is abandoned, and its own decoder runs only when explicitly enabled; its default API route delegates to ext/json. JSON Machine shares ext/json for member decoding. salsify accepts only object/array roots and silently accepts concatenated documents, so its harness rejects anything other than one complete document; the tree-building listener is harness code. The own-parser lead joelwurtz/json-stream-polyfill and three low-download supplemental hits remain uninspected. bcncommerce/json-stream (lossy Reader, identical package lines on both controls) and symfony/json-streamer (a schema-free read is one json_decode call) are excluded after pinned probes; salsify forks and listener wrappers and json_decode wrappers, including colinodell/json5 on both valid controls, are excluded. pcrov/jsonreader has a separate lexer and state machine, with three parser-source features and AFL tuples differing between the valid controls. boundwize/jsonrecast builds a formatting-preserving AST with its own lexer and recursive-descent parser; string escapes are ext/json on single tokens, and most of its 35-line control differential is in the indentation-detection pass that parse() runs. laktak/hjson parses a JSON superset and is counted only for valid JSON; it drops an empty member name and lets duplicates overwrite by source reading. klkvsk/json-decode-stream unescapes string tokens with ext/json and accepts concatenated documents, which its adapter rejects. eftec/services_json returns null rather than an error for text it cannot reduce, and its 4-line control differential is the smallest among the selected PHP JSON paths. The bounded search used thirteen Packagist queries of at most 100 hits each: five captured at 03:23 UTC and eight supplemental queries (json stream, json5, jsonc, json lexer, json tokenizer, json reader, hjson, json pull parser) captured at 15:19 UTC. Packagist matches json5, jsonc and hjson loosely, so their first 100 hits are mostly generic JSON packages. Rankings use the 03:23 download values, which cover every selected path. Package downloads measure overall/historical adoption, not JSON parsing frequency. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Ten positive-signal Python JSON third-party paths pass valid nested object and array controls with source-level parser coverage and AFL++ feedback: pydantic 2.14.3 (1,139,429,690 PyPI Stats last-month downloads), jiter 0.19.0 (421,162,504), orjson 3.13.0 (218,014,317), json5 0.17.3 (50,036,028), simplejson 4.3.0 (49,365,386), ijson 3.6.0 (46,615,664), msgspec 0.22.0 (39,138,375), ujson 6.1.0 (29,543,889), dirtyjson 1.0.8 (5,671,026) and hjson 3.1.0 (4,411,122). Pydantic embeds Jiter 0.18.0; standalone jiter uses Jiter 0.19.0 through a distinct package API. These are shared-family paths, not independent parsers, and their package downloads are not combined; orjson shares the yyjson C syntax-parser family but this pilot measures its Rust deserializer, not vendored C source lines. ijson uses the asserted yajl2_c backend, with pinned YAJL C tokenizer and Python extension coverage; its source-built embedded YAJL -O0 route differs from the official Linux wheel linkage and optimisation, and its other backends are untested. msgspec uses its own C JSON decoder in _core.c through untyped msgspec.json.decode; its source-built clang -O0 path differs from the official GCC wheel, typed decoding is untested, and JSON decoder sections are counted separately from other codecs in the same file. ujson uses its own UltraJSON C decoder with vendored double-conversion C++ for fractional numbers; both controls equal an exact CPython json oracle tree, and duplicate-key and edge-number behavior is recorded from source, not tested. json5 is a pure-Python JSON5 superset parser (glop-generated PEG parser.py plus lib.py conversion) that never calls the standard json module; json5.loads on bytes, on text and json5.load on a stream give the exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree for both controls, with 668 covered package lines and stable feedback differing by 27 parser.py lines and 27 AFL++ tuples. It accepts JSON5-only syntax, so it does not reject non-RFC 8259 input, and its downloads mainly reflect JSON5 configuration use. dirtyjson and hjson are pure-Python decoders of simplejson-derived lineage (dirtyjson calls its loader a drastic rewrite of the simplejson loader; hjson says it is based on simplejson), so with the selected simplejson path they form one shared lineage of three separate code bases, not three independent parsers. dirtyjson.loads and hjson.loads on bytes and text, and their load on a stream, give the exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree for both controls with the standard json module blocked; dirtyjson covers 156 package lines (129 in loader.py) with stable feedback differing by 14 lines and 14 AFL++ tuples, hjson 159 lines (152 in decoder.py) differing by 4 lines and 4 tuples. Both accept non-RFC 8259 input (dirtyjson is lenient, hjson parses the Hjson superset), and their downloads include non-JSON configuration and extraction use. The bounded PyPI Simple index search (six project-name queries, first 100 alphabetical hits each) and a top-15,000 download list used only as a discovery aid added 22 leads. json5, dirtyjson and hjson were promoted; 9 are excluded (json-repair returns the standard json.loads result on valid input and documents its own repair parser, skip_json_loads=True, only for input known to be invalid; pydantic-core is the same binary as the pydantic path; pandas, pyarrow and polars are tabular readers; srsly, partial-json-parser and commentjson delegate to ujson or CPython json; jsonnet evaluates a language) and 10 remain unresolved, all with fewer downloads than hjson, the tenth selected path, so none could enter the ten-path ceiling. python-rapidjson 1.26 (4,066,455) and pysimdjson 8.0.0 (679,340) passed every gate as selected paths but were displaced by dirtyjson and hjson under the ten-path ceiling; their catalog rows, verification records and receipts are kept in ceiling-displaced.json. These ten are not a definitive top ten by the metric. Python standard json is separately verified.

Ten verified Rust JSON parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (600 hits, 476 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Ten documented leads remain unverified, so this is a bounded pilot rather than a complete top-ten ranking. ijson 0.1.7 was excluded after source inspection: it has an IValue type deserialized through serde_json::from_slice and no own local JSON parser API. Downloads are 90-day adoption proxies that include transitive pulls. Two small valid controls establish only observed RFC 8259 structure; duplicate keys, huge numbers, deep nesting and non-UTF-8 are untested.

Two verified paths from two independent decoder families; no lower-ranked filler entries. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad needs MAD_BUFFER_GUARD (8) zero bytes appended after the input; the harness adds exactly that and counts every recoverable error except the one LOSTSYNC at the guard. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for whole distributions (the mpg123 player and library; the mad formula library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c, and libmad is the decoder behind the SoX path there. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Seven verified Go plain-MP3 paths; korandiz/mpa v1.0.0 is excluded by a pinned valid MPEG-2 control that yields zero frames and unexpected EOF, matching its MPEG-1-only header check; no padding. Five pkg.go.dev queries were bounded at 100 hits each (313 hits, 242 unique). Every hit with at least two Imported by packages is now a selected path or a recorded lead. Of the 13 one-importer hits, only sdobz/go-mpg123, a distinct decoder family, is recorded; the others were judged from path and synopsis only (go-mp3 or tcolgate forks by name, tag readers, a video converter, and HLS or livego copies). 39 leads are recorded: five remain unresolved (go-mp3 wrappers pipelined.dev/audio/mp3 and qiniu/audio/mp3, tcolgate wrapper sa6mwa/mp3duration, cgo minimp3 binding cowork-ai/go-minimp3 and cgo libmpg123 wrapper sdobz/go-mpg123, none harnessed), and three are unselected shared-family forks or wrappers. derat/mpeg and mattetti/audio/mp3 parse both valid controls correctly but are excluded by the feedback gate, because each control pair covers identical parser blocks. fgergo/mp3 is a byte-identical fork of tcolgate/mp3 (15 of 16 files identical) and is not counted. pkg.go.dev Imported by counts package adoption rather than MP3-specific use, and wrapper counts are not independent decoder adoption. The hajimehoshi/go-mp3 and tcolgate/mp3 families are also represented in the tagged MP3 cell; the plain-frame routes are separate format paths, not new cross-cell families. Two untagged constant-bitrate controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, other MPEG layers, or ID3 handling. minimp3 PCM hashes are pinned to the Clang-built linux/arm64 image, and Beep float64 sample hashes to their go-mp3 release on linux/arm64; neither is compared across toolchains or releases.

Five pure-Java Layer III paths verified; no padding. jaudiotagger is first-header-only and mp3agic reports only accurate header fields. Both higher-level APIs misidentify the valid 22.05 kHz control start at byte 104 and estimate 5 rather than 12 frames; mp3agic reports 261 ms versus oracle about 313 ms. These paths make no whole-file frame-count or duration claim. JavaMP3 1.0.1 decodes the mono control exactly but crashes on valid 22.05 kHz stereo input, so is excluded with a reproducible probe. Maven Central phrase queries returned no hits, so named leads were inspected via deps.dev and package documentation. deps.dev counts whole-package dependency use, not MP3-specific calls. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or ID3 behavior. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 reader by inventory.

Five verified paths; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Download counts cover whole toolkits: mediabunny's muxing, conversion and many containers, and codec-parser's AAC, FLAC and Ogg parsers, not MP3 framing alone. The first three remain the highest-download fetched candidates; mp3-duration and mp3-parser have lower adoption. mp3-parser has 40,519 monthly downloads, below the duration-only leads, and is selected for its documented frame reader and exact whole-control walk. Its AFL++ differential is narrow: two source ranges in lib.js octetToBinRep bit extraction, not distinct version/channel branches. None decodes Layer III audio. The mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5, CRC-protected or ID3 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists. codec-parser's valid-control AFL++ differential is narrow: one header-cache range that tracks distinct frame headers, not version or channel branches. Its V8 line counts include module evaluation of imported AAC, FLAC, Opus, Vorbis and Ogg files that audio/mpeg parsing does not call. music-metadata reports MPEG version and layer only through its codec string ('MPEG 1 Layer 3'), not as separate fields, and needs duration: true for a full frame walk. Its valid-control AFL++ differential is 4 sync() tail-policy ranges that track frame length, not version or channel branches. Its V8 package line count (3,539) is mostly module evaluation; MpegParser.js alone is 245 lines. mp3-duration exposes only duration; its count-scoped AFL signal tracks 11 versus 12 frame calls and may reflect input length, not a new branch or line. The same release is also verified for tagged MP3 duration in the ID3v2 cell.

Two verified paths; no padding. Search is seven Packagist search.json queries capped at 50 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; package descriptions alone decided most exclusions. Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 or Mp3Info transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate. Mp3Info reads two headers, estimates frames from audio bytes and the computed frame length, and reports duration one frame short ((frames - 1) x 1152 / sample rate). On the MPEG-2 control it uses the MPEG-1 frame-length coefficient, misses the third frame and reads a false sync at byte 236, reporting Layer II 24 kHz mono 96 kbit/s; MPEG-2 is not covered for Mp3Info. Neither path decodes audio. PHP-MP3 (falahati/php-mp3) failed the controls: the v0.9.5-alpha2 tag does not return on PHP 8.5, and the dev-master snapshot reads the MPEG-2 control as 3 frames at 11,025 Hz (data/php/mp3/falahati-php-mp3-control-audit.md). No lead remains unresolved (data/php/mp3/lead-audit.md). debach/zend-mp3 1.8.1 walks MPEG frames itself in Zend_Media_Mpeg_Abs, but its parent class file does not compile on PHP 8 (removed $str{$i} offsets), so it returns nothing on PHP 8.5. fobilow/mp3file has no release tag or license and also fails to compile. The re-scan found a native MPEG-1 Layer III decoder in xiaosongshu/flv2mp4 v1.8.7: 12,672 samples at 44.1 kHz on the MPEG-1 control, no frames on the MPEG-2 control, and its documented API decodes in a child process. holine/mp3 copies PHP-MP3 and does not return on either control. wapmorgan/media-file, dgoriaev/mp3info and acekyd/laravelmp3 delegate to or copy Mp3Info or getID3; phpvideotoolkit, mediaprobe, mp3php and soundfile hand parsing to FFmpeg or libsndfile. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Three verified paths; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. eyed3 and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. TinyTag also only reads headers: after five equal-bitrate frames it estimates duration from stream size and mean frame length, and it does not expose MPEG version, layer or frame count. Both full-length controls run the same TinyTag lines; its feedback difference is shown with a valid three-frame prefix of the 44.1 kHz control. hachoir is called through its MpegAudioFile class directly, not guessParser, whose fallback tries every hachoir parser in set order. It walks every frame header to EOF and reports version, layer, sample rate, bitrate, channel mode and frame count. It does not decode audio or side information, and its two controls differ by only 4 mpeg_audio.py lines: the MPEG-1 versus MPEG-2 bitrate table and frame-length formula. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Six verified package paths cover four parser families on two valid untagged CBR controls: Symphonia's Rust MP3 demuxer/decoder, reached directly through symphonia-bundle-mp3 and through the symphonia facade's probe and codec registry; minimp3's C decoder through the Rust minimp3 binding and as the pure-Rust nanomp3 port; the mp3-duration frame-header scanner, which reports only a summed duration; rusty_mp3's in-house pure-Rust Layer III decoder. The symphonia facade is a separate package API over the same Symphonia family, not a new engine; nanomp3 is a separate package API over the minimp3 family (its minimp3-compatible PCM is byte-identical to scalar minimp3.h), and nanomp3-core, the decoder it re-exports, is counted only through nanomp3. Five leads remain unresolved, so the verified ranks are not a claim about all MP3 parsers. Search covers the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. The two controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II or MPEG-2.5 support.

Pilot cell: five third-party paths. expat 2.10.0, libxml2 2.15.4 and Mini-XML 4.0.6 were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. libxmlb 0.3.30 (over GLib 2.88.4's GMarkup) builds a silo from both controls and matches the expat non-namespace summary as a raw-name path: names as written, xmlns declarations as attributes, no namespace URIs. Its 1,381 covered libxmlb lines and 604 GMarkup lines on the first control, and an allowlisted AFL++ map (gmarkup.c and libxmlb's xb-*.c only, checked with nm) of 639 vs 653 tuples with 32 differing, are stable. GMarkup is a documented XML subset parser; libxmlb drops comments and processing instructions. libnxml 0.18.6 matches the same raw-name summary; its own namespace pass binds unprefixed attributes to the default namespace, so its URIs are not reported, and the adapter re-joins libnxml's stored prefix and local name. 720 libnxml lines are covered (346 in nxml_parser.c) and its AFL++ map (393 vs 426 tuples, 53 differing) is stable. libnxml0t64's 104 installations are a very weak signal. The five paths are distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie. libxmlb2 is a dependency of fwupd and AppStream tooling, so its count reflects those installations. The Debian sourcemax table would invert the first two (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. mxml's value is the 3.x soname libmxml1; the pinned 4.0.6 is Debian forky/sid's mxml source. Mini-XML does not implement Namespaces in XML: it returns prefix:local names and keeps xmlns declarations as attributes, so its expanded names, declaration counts and URIs are computed by the adapter from mxml's tree, not by the package. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search: the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits), seven targeted C names, every Debian source name containing 'xml' in the hashed sourcemax snapshot (306 hits, 5 of them C XML parser libraries: libxml2.9, libxml2, libxmlb, mxml, libnxml; all classified in the registry snapshot) and seven targeted Debian sources. GLib's GMarkup is unranked: glib2.0 builds all of GLib and Debian has no GMarkup-specific development package. iksemel (libiksemel3 4,375, source no longer in Debian) fails the second valid control: it maps character references to '?' and leaves attribute entities undecoded. libgsf, qdbm, xmlrpc-c, xmlrpc-epi, libstrophe and wbxml2 are wrappers, tokenizers or protocol libraries. Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The namespace control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) and the raw-name oracles use Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not the others. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

All five C++ XML paths pass the namespace-aware catalog control with source coverage and AFL++ feedback. Xerces-C++, pugixml, libxml++ and RapidXML pass the shared second valid control; TinyXML2 uses a no-processing-instruction variant because it rejects that instruction, while RapidXML's default flags skip it. libxml++ parser-only feedback and native libxml2 parser.c lines are repeatable and input-dependent. The bounded search covered five named format-specific libraries, so other C++ XML packages remain unmeasured. Homebrew install-on-request orders the first three differently and its libxml++ formula is an older ABI; RapidXML has no Homebrew formula. The libxml++ 275 Debian dev installs sum three ABIs, while its matching ABI-5 package has seven. RapidXML's 17 librapidxml-dev installations, none with recent use, are a weak adoption signal and exclude vendored or Boost-embedded copies. Two small valid UTF-8 controls cannot establish complete XML 1.0, DTD/entity, encoding or malformed-input behavior.

Seven Go XML package paths pass two valid namespace-aware controls with parser-source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback: etree 2,098; xmlquery 627; mxj 553; beego/x2j 436; govmomi/vim25/xml 163; goxpp 132; gokogiri/xml 108 Imported by. The first four and goxpp use the Go encoding/xml runtime tokenizer through package-specific tree, map or cursor APIs. govmomi/vim25/xml contains its own compiled tokenizer fork of Go encoding/xml; the pinned v0.56.2 package imports no runtime encoding/xml and covers 290 own xml.go lines. Its parser-only AFL feedback differs by 30 fork-source blocks on the valid controls with stable repeats. Its source is a 12,553,438-byte whole govmomi module archive, though the XML package itself is much smaller. Higher-adoption goxml2json (182) and mxj/v2 (178), plus six other numeric leads, remain unverified; ranks cover selected verified paths only. mxj and x2j map routes lose namespace URIs/prefixes and mixed-content details; x2j byte/string routes alter CDATA whitespace on the valid catalog control, while its selected reader route preserves it. Gokogiri is a cgo DOM binding over pinned libxml2 2.15.4 with 93 Go binding and 1,730 native parser source lines covered; parser-only AFL feedback differs between the controls and is stable over five repeats. Pilot cell with ten verified third-party paths: saxes 6.0.0, jsdom 31.0.1, sax 1.6.1, fast-xml-parser 5.12.1, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12, xml2js 0.6.2, xml-js 1.6.11, htmlparser2 12.0.0 xmlMode, xmldoc 3.0.0, and @xml-tools/parser 1.0.12 are control-verified, source-covered, and have input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Comparable 30-day npm downloads rank the ten package paths; counts include transitive adoption. The ten paths cover six independent parser families: jsdom shares saxes and xml2js shares sax. saxes and sax share historical fork lineage but have distinct parser code. fast-xml-parser has its own scanner and validator but no namespace URI resolution, so the adapter resolves expanded names over its qualified names and xmlns attributes. @xmldom/xmldom has its own XMLReader tokenizer and DOM builder, accepts locally decoded text, and the adapter treats every warning or error as fatal. jsdom builds its XML DOM over the same pinned saxes 6.0.0 tokenizer as the selected saxes path; it copies DOCTYPE entity declarations into saxes and forces XML 1.0 rules, and its AFL++ feedback includes input-independent window setup alongside saxes and DOM construction. xml2js, xml-js and xmldoc build distinct trees over the same pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer as the selected sax path; it drops comments and processing instructions, which can merge adjacent text segments. Wrapper package and underlying tokenizer source coverage are recorded separately. xmlbuilder2 4.0.3 is excluded from this namespace-aware selection: its native DOM misassigns the c:catalog and c:lang namespace URIs on the valid catalog control; the adapter does not repair them. htmlparser2 xmlMode has its own forgiving tokenizer but no XML well-formedness or namespace-URI enforcement; it is selected only as a raw-name XML event path, and its 526,964,241 downloads mostly measure HTML use. xmldoc builds a raw-name tree over sax; it omits prolog comments and PIs. Both are compared only to a non-namespace Expat oracle projected to preserved fields, without adapter-side namespace repair. @xml-tools/parser returns a raw-QName Chevrotain CST without namespace URI expansion or decoded entity text; the Expat raw-name hierarchy matches both controls, and parser ALT callback hit-count feedback changes on 11 ranges while ordinary covered-line sets do not. The search is bounded to recorded queries and snapshot; two valid controls do not establish complete XML 1.0 compliance.

Pilot cell, seven verified third-party paths. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler was reassessed under the same wrapper rule and counted: its package-own scope is Crawler navigation and XPath/namespace mapping over a libxml2 DOMDocument, not tokenizing, and its Xdebug package lines differ by only one post-parse line between the two controls, so its AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay (source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4, allowlist limited to libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c and ext/dom document.c plus ext/libxml) running the same Crawler harness, where the controls differ in 357 stable tuples, all arising while addXmlContent parses; its downloads are mostly HTML crawling uses. jms/serializer stays excluded because it maps an already parsed SimpleXML tree onto a target class model. symfony/serializer maps a DOMDocument through XmlEncoder::decode; its Xdebug package lines are separate from 359 stable native parser-time AFL tuples, and its whole-component downloads mostly reflect other encoders. It drops the root name and descendant namespace declarations. veewee/xml preserves qualified names and per-element xmlns declarations but groups siblings; mtownsend/xml-to-array loses namespace URIs, declarations and attribute prefixes. Both have package-owned array mapping and parser-only native libxml2 AFL feedback, not new tokenizer families. prewk/xml-string-streamer is excluded after a pinned two-control probe showed raw byte slicing only. laravie/parser is excluded because Reader::load is simplexml_load_file and Document::parse only maps that tree onto a caller schema, similar to excluded jms/serializer. saloonphp/xml-wrangler parses twice through veewee XMLReader and DOMDocument; its raw-name Element DTO loses namespace URI resolution and the nested empty-default undeclaration on the valid order control. Its 414 stable native AFL tuples are parser-derived, while package-own Xdebug lines are separate. pear/xml_parser (XML_Parser 1.3.8, abandoned on Packagist, last release 2019) is counted as a libxml2-family SAX package path: it creates and configures the ext/xml parser itself (xml_parser_create without a namespace separator, case folding, handler binding, string or 4096-byte stream feeding, free), so its raw-name summary is checked against an expat non-namespace oracle, with xmlns declarations as attributes and the documented $folding property set to false. Its coverage image source-builds PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4 with Xdebug 3.5.3 and LLVM coverage, so one run records 56 package lines plus ext/xml and libxml2 lines. Like laravie/parser, every AFL tuple that differs between its controls (299) also differs under a bare xml_parser_create/xml_parse baseline with the same handler object; unlike laravie, its own role is driving the parse rather than mapping an already parsed tree, so it is selected with that limit stated. PHP 8.5 deprecates its xml_set_object() and xml_parser_free() calls; the notices are recorded. orchestra/parser is excluded with laravie/parser: its pinned source only extends laravie's Reader and Document with Laravel container wiring. jtrumbull/xml-parser is excluded after a pinned probe showed decode() is a bare SimpleXML JSON round trip. The smaller libxml2-family wrappers (alex.oleshkevich/fast-xml-parser, atk14/xmole, arc/xml) remain unresolved, as does the own-code lead watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Both coverage images use Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; both AFL++ overlays use the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE. Standard paths: XMLReader::XML, DOMDocument::loadXML, simplexml_load_string and xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse are four PHP 8.5.12 runtime APIs over the same source-built libxml2 2.15.4, counted separately from the third-party paths and not ranked; DOMDocument::loadXML and simplexml_load_string take the control as an in-memory string, and their AFL++ overlays instrument only libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/dom document.c or ext/simplexml simplexml.c. SimpleXML exposes no separate text nodes, so its summary merges mixed-content character data per element (neither control has any); simplexml.c also holds the traversal methods, which the parse-only fuzz target does not call. xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse is the only push-parser entry point (xmlCreatePushParserCtxt/xmlParseChunk through ext/xml/compat.c's expat-style SAX callbacks, no tree); its summary comes from event handlers with case folding off and a "\x01" namespace separator, the controls go in one final chunk, and its AFL++ overlay instruments libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/xml xml.c and compat.c. ext/xml has no comment handler (comments reach the default handler) and reports user-defined entity references unexpanded to the default handler, which the harness rejects.

Seven verified third-party paths (lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml, xmltodict, xmlschema, parsel and untangle) are selected from nine named PyPI/project-documentation leads. A bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending; 2 leads are unresolved, so this is not a completed top-ten ranking. lxml uses source-built libxml2 2.15.4; beautifulsoup4's documented 'xml' builder runs on the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared parser family, no independent XML tokenizer, recover=True); xmltodict, defusedxml (guarded pure-Python ElementTree XMLParser), untangle (SAX via defusedxml's DefusedExpatParser) and the standard ElementTree path use Expat. defusedxml is a guard facade over CPython ElementTree, not an independent XML engine; its own code is constant on the valid controls, and ElementTree keeps no xmlns declarations, so its comparison with the lxml oracle omits the declaration count. untangle runs SAX without namespace processing and drops namespace URIs; its controls are checked against an lxml oracle projected to untangle's qualified-name view, not against namespace-expanded names. The lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml and untangle controls exercise valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 namespace structures without DOCTYPE, not full XML conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use; Beautiful Soup downloads are mostly HTML use, and defusedxml downloads are largely transitive. lxml, beautifulsoup4 and parsel AFL feedback excludes parser.c lines 8700-8720 because address-sensitive attribute hash lookups varied across identical valid replays. xmlschema's XMLResource is not an independent XML engine: it consumes CPython's default xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse events over the C _elementtree parser, pyexpat and Expat 2.10.0. It records xmlns declarations and per-element namespace maps itself, so its controls match the lxml path's full summary including the declaration count; its own 110 lines are the same on both controls and only their hit counts differ. xmlschema downloads are mostly XSD validation use. parsel's documented Selector(body=bytes, type='xml') is not an independent XML tokenizer: it strips the body and NUL bytes and calls lxml.etree.fromstring with SafeXMLParser(recover=True, resolve_entities=False, huge_tree=True) over the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared lxml/libxml2 family). Both valid controls match an independent CPython pyexpat oracle. Parsel's own 100 selector.py lines are the same on both controls, so its input-dependent AFL++ feedback (209 tuples) comes entirely from libxml2 parser.c. Parsel downloads are mostly Scrapy HTML scraping use.

Ten verified XML parser paths selected, reaching the cell ceiling, within the first 100 hits of seven crates.io queries (642 hits, 483 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Six documented leads remain unverified and were not run after the tenth slot was filled. xmltree, serde-xml-rs, elementtree and treexml fall outside the first 100 hits of the recorded queries, so they have no snapshot metric and were not ranked; a live crates.io lookup on 2026-11-17 showed xmltree and elementtree (both xml-rs family) with more recent downloads than instant-xml, so a broader search could change the tenth slot. xml5ever 0.40.0 is an XML5 error-recovering superset parser: the two valid XML 1.0 controls verify namespace-aware output, but it does not establish strict XML 1.0 well-formedness, complete namespace behavior, DTD support, or other encodings. rxml 0.14.0 is a deliberately restricted XML 1.0 parser without DTDs, custom entities or processing instructions, and it rejects comments by default. It parses the shared catalog control exactly but rejects the shared order control (Error(RestrictedXml("comments"))), so its second control is order-default-ns-restricted.xml without that comment and processing instruction. The xml-rs 1.0.0 package is a compatibility re-export of xml and excluded as a duplicate family. minidom 0.19.0 is a DOM wrapper over the selected rxml family: rxml's RawReader lexes and parses, and minidom's own TreeBuilder resolves prefixes and builds the tree. It inherits rxml's restricted subset, so it also rejects the shared order control and uses the restricted order control; its stable AFL++ edge differential has no change in minidom source-line counts, and the differing lines are in rxml. uppsala 0.12.1 parses both shared valid controls through its own namespace-aware DOM parser; the controls do not establish its XPath, XSD or XSLT features, DTD handling, other encodings, or complete XML 1.0 conformance. Downloads include transitive pulls and are adoption proxies; ranks compare selected paths only, and the minidom and rxml counts overlap because minidom depends on rxml. RustyXML 0.3.0 parses both shared valid controls through its own ObjFW-derived streaming parser; its README lists incomplete error checking, so the controls do not establish strict XML 1.0 well-formedness checking, DTD handling or non-UTF-8 encodings. Its AFL++ overlay fixes std HashMap RandomState keys with a getrandom AFL_PRELOAD shim; see data/rust/xml/rustyxml-feedback-audit.md. instant-xml 0.7.7 is a typed mapping library over the selected xmlparser tokenizer; only its generic AnyElement view is tested. It consumes xmlns declarations without exposing them, so its summary omits the declaration count; AnyElement keeps only the last text node per element; it rejects the processing instruction inside the shared order control's root, so its second control is order-default-ns-no-pi.xml.
